summary: Routing hygiene break during canary consolidation causes mixed pinned-model assignments
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary consolidation for NovaDocs (dedicated pool in us-east-1), several tenant sessions reported unexpected model flips: pinned sessions that were explicitly pinned to the promoted variant started routing intermittently to the older compatibility quantized variant. This resulted in mixed outputs and a small burst of higher token latency for affected customers.

Impact:
- NovaDocs reported ~2% of requests in a 15-minute window returned responses from the legacy quantized variant instead of the promoted variant.
- Affected requests saw a median latency increase of ~250ms and tokenization deltas for some prompt templates.
- No 5xx spike, but model-quality regressions for pinned sessions; customer halted traffic to the affected route as a precaution.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: redwood-dedicated-us-east-03
- Canary consolidation operation initiated: 2026-03-10 01:12 UTC
- Canaries involved: redwood/gpt-neox-20b-v2 (promoted) and redwood/gpt-neox-20b-quant-compat (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer pins session to promoted variant via API with model pin headers.
2) During consolidation window (canary weight shift + snapshot merge), some sessions receive 200 OK but response has headers indicating fallback-variant: redwood/gpt-neox-20b-quant-compat.
3) Replaying requests from affected session tokens locally against production snapshot reproduces the mixed-routing in ~1 out of 50 attempts.

Observed behavior:
- Pin metadata stamped at edge showed expected promoted-variant token, but orchestrator routing decision sometimes consulted an out-of-date snapshot shard for cohort mapping.
- Edge->orchestrator trace shows a 15–40ms delay where a merge worker was writing epoch data; during that window the routing decision fell back to a compatibility lookup path that prefers an available instance (older variant).

Expected behavior:
- Pinned sessions must maintain strict affinity to the pinned variant until explicit unpin or TTL expiry; consolidation should not cause transient routing to fallback variant for pinned sessions.

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support instructed NovaDocs to enable their tenant-level explicit hold (tenant-override = true) to force strict affinity; this prevented further incorrect routing while we investigated.
- Orchestrator team applied a short lock-step patch to serialize snapshot-finalize and routing-read for pinned cohorts (hotfix queued).

Investigation notes:
- Correlated edge request IDs with orchestrator logs (trace IDs: trace/20260310-01-{A..F}).
- Found race in snapshot merge: snapshot-merge job completed but its commit-notify to the routing cache service could be delayed when merge worker GC overlapped with final commit. During that delay, routing cache served a fallback code path that used instance-availability heuristics (and ignored explicit pin lease for a small subset of cohort keys).
- Reproducer indicates probability increases when merge worker CPU spikes coincide with a GC pause on the merge node.
- Related PRs identified which touched routing cache invalidation: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821 (merge orchestration) and https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4899 (cache optimization). Both are linked for context.

Next steps and owner assignments:
- Omar (Orchestrator) to push the staged hotfix that reorders commit-notify before deallocating merge worker resources (ETA 2026-03-12 06:00 UTC).
- SRE (Maya) to monitor merge-worker GC metrics across us-east dedicated clusters and add a short-term alert when GC pause > 80ms during commit windows.
- DX (Leah) to coordinate with NovaDocs for gradual unhold and a short verification run once hotfix is live.

Notes on customer communication:
- We informed NovaDocs of the temporary tenant-override instruction and that a targeted hotfix is in progress.
- Promised a full post-incident write-up after root-cause verification and rollout of longer-term guardrails.
